mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS decline is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained inflation rate crossing above 2.0% triggers investor concerns about future rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns do not turn negative despite inflation crossing above 2.0% or the effect fades within the period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer demand (GDPC1) creates conflicting signals, but their combined effect during a 60-day period typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not rise significantly despite both proxies moving in the expected direction or their combined effect is neutral.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (e.g., rising federal funds rates), investors anticipate higher interest rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during identified tightening periods or the rate increase does not align with market expectations.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in the unemployment rate below 5.0% signals labor market tightness, prompting concerns about wage pressures and inflation, which drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not turn negative despite UNRATE falling below 5.0% or the effect dissipates quickly.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both consumer demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns do not rise significantly despite both proxies increasing or their combined effect is neutral.

mechanism_narrative: Consistent upward momentum in employment (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, fostering confidence and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns fail to rise significantly despite sustained employment growth or the effect fades over time.

mechanism_narrative: A late-cycle peak in industrial production (INDPRO) combined with monetary easing (FEDFUNDS) creates uncertainty about future growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not turn negative despite INDPRO peaking or the effect fades within the period.
